_documentation.about: This file can be edited or copied to preconfigure Dayglance before launch. The _documentation section is explanatory and ignored by the app.

locations.meaning: defaultLocation is the first area shown. locations are additional swipeable areas. Use null and an empty list to ask for a location on first launch.
locations.validInputs: For a searched location, provide query as a city, region, or postal code; countryCode is an optional ISO country code such as US. For a fixed location, provide numeric latitude and longitude instead. Each id must be unique.

returnAfterSeconds.meaning: Idle time before the hourly view closes; defaults to 60 seconds and 0 keeps it open.

radarIdleTimeoutSeconds.meaning: Inactivity time before the precipitation map closes; defaults to 60 seconds. Touch, pointer, keyboard, and map scrolling reset the timer.

temperatureUnit.meaning: Temperature display and forecast request units.

measurementSystem.meaning: Wind, pressure, visibility, and precipitation units.

refreshMinutes.meaning: How often the forecast is refreshed.

temperatureGraphRange.meaning: Temperature graph period: day shows the next 24 hours, week shows 7 forecast days, forecast16 shows up to 16 forecast days, and history30 shows the previous 30 days ending today.

examples.history30: Past 30 days of historical weather, not a forecast

autoScrollLocations.meaning: Automatically advance through saved locations when more than one exists; the cycle loops between locations and does not open the add-location page.

autoScrollIntervalSeconds.meaning: Time to show each location before smoothly advancing. This timer is only used when autoScrollLocations is true.

showBumpers.meaning: Show optional previous/next buttons below the hourly cards; disabled by default. The cards remain swipeable when false.

alertsEnabled.meaning: Show active National Weather Service alerts for the currently displayed U.S. location. This is an on-screen supplement, not an emergency alert system.

alertMinimumSeverity.meaning: Minimum NWS alert severity to show. Unrated alerts are always included so missing severity metadata does not hide a potentially important alert.

startup.autoStart: True starts Dayglance at desktop login; enabling it in local Pi Settings installs the login hook automatically. For JSON-only setup, run install-autostart.sh once. False leaves it off.
startup.kiosk: true opens Chromium in full-screen kiosk mode; false opens a maximized window.

radar.meaning: The optional radar uses RainViewer for the past and Rainbow Weather for forecast tiles. RainViewer requires no key. Rainbow credentials are device-local and must never be placed in this public config file.
radar.setup: Create a Rainbow developer account, then enter its API key in Settings > Radar & Provider Account on the Pi's local screen.
radar.paidUsage: Pay-as-you-go is disabled by default. Enable it explicitly in the local settings UI after checking the Rainbow account dashboard. The local free-allowance stop only counts this Dayglance server.
radar.documentation: See RADAR.md for current free allowances, provider usage tracking, and pay-as-you-go rates.

weatherAlerts.meaning: Free, active National Weather Service point alerts for U.S. locations. The dashboard checks only the currently displayed city every five minutes and caches the result in memory. No API key is required. The colored status indicator reports feed connectivity, not alert severity.
weatherAlerts.settings: Enable or disable alerts and set the minimum severity in Settings > Connections & Alerts > Severe Weather Alerts.
weatherAlerts.limits: Alerts for locations outside the United States are not currently supported. Dayglance uses a five-minute pull interval and is not a push notification or emergency warning service. Keep official phone/NOAA Weather Radio alerts enabled.

stationIntegrations.meaning: Each saved city may use at most one optional current-observation source. Integrations are separate from the forecast provider. Supported connections are Ambient Weather local-upload/cloud-api and Weather Underground cloud-api. Settings assigns each configured source to one saved city.
stationIntegrations.connection: For local-upload, send Ambient Weather-native or Weather Underground-compatible uploads to stationReceiver. Ambient cloud-api reads the latest data from Ambient Weather's REST API; Weather Underground cloud-api reads the latest PWS observation from The Weather Company API. Both cloud adapters use device-local credentials and all connections leave the forecast source unchanged.
stationIntegrations.validInputs: Each enabled entry needs a unique id and staleAfterSeconds from 30 to 3600. Ambient local-upload needs provider ambient-weather, connection local-upload, and private IPv4 sourceIp. Ambient cloud-api needs provider ambient-weather, connection cloud-api, a 12-digit hexadecimal deviceId, and credentialsId. Weather Underground cloud-api needs provider weather-underground, connection cloud-api, stationId, and credentialsId. Credentials live in device-station-credentials.json, never in config.json. locationId may be null; associate the city in Settings.
stationIntegrations.limits: Local upload requires a DHCP reservation/static private IP and a LAN-only listener; never forward its port publicly. Ambient cloud polling makes one request per configured account per minute, below its published request rate. Weather Underground PWS cloud access requires an authorized Weather Company API key; trial quotas and paid limits depend on current provider terms. Samples are not archived and clear from memory on a service restart.

stationReceiver.meaning: Network listener shared by enabled local station integrations. It accepts only the configured upload path and allowlisted private source IPs.
stationReceiver.validInputs: bindAddress must be the Pi's specific private IPv4 address (not 0.0.0.0 or loopback); port must be 1024-65535. Keep the default path unless the station upload form requires another one.
stationReceiver.restart: After changing stationReceiver or adding/enabling an integration in config.json, restart the Dayglance service. The browser Settings association applies immediately without a restart.
